summary: Ocean Software became one of the most visible British computer-game publishers of the 1980s and early 1990s. Its CCG archive is particularly strong in arcade conversions, film licences and large boxed releases that helped define the UK retail scene.
note: The archive treats each credited publishing label separately, even where staff, licences or distribution relationships overlapped.

summary: Mastertronic was central to the British budget-game market, placing inexpensive releases in newsagents and high-street shops and giving many C64 owners a large library without full-price spending.
note: Related Mastertronic labels remain separate so their individual game credits can still be explored.

summary: Firebird was one of Telecomsoft's best-known labels and covered both inexpensive releases and more ambitious full-price games. The label is remembered for a broad C64 catalogue and distinctive packaging.
note: Firebird, Rainbird and later associated labels are kept as separate archive destinations.

summary: US Gold brought a substantial number of American and arcade properties to European home-computer owners. Its catalogue spans sports, action games, conversions and licensed releases across both C64 and Amiga.
note: Re-release labels are linked only where they exist as separate publisher routes in the CCG archive.

summary: Codemasters built a major reputation through affordable, technically confident games and recognisable series. The C64 catalogue includes racing, sports, platform and arcade-style releases.
note: The publisher page reflects the credits in the main CCG game database rather than every title released on other systems.

summary: System 3 became closely associated with polished action-adventure releases and strong presentation on the Commodore 64. Several of its games remain among the machine's most discussed later-1980s releases.
note: Publishing and development credits can differ between territories and versions; this page follows the archive's recorded publisher fields.

summary: Activision's Commodore catalogue ranges from early home-computer releases to licensed action games and distributed European titles. It is one of the larger publisher collections in the CCG archive.
note: Some games carried different publishers by territory; the CCG page lists the credits stored for each archived version.

summary: Electronic Arts published a wide mixture of sports, simulations, construction tools and original computer games. Its C64 and Amiga output includes both accessible arcade-style titles and much deeper disk-based releases.
note: Developer and publisher relationships are shown separately wherever the archive contains both credits.

summary: Psygnosis became strongly associated with visually ambitious Amiga games, elaborate packaging and a distinctive science-fiction and fantasy identity.
note: The CCG archive currently represents only the games already covered on the site, not Psygnosis's complete commercial catalogue.

summary: Elite Systems was a major British publisher of arcade conversions and licensed action games. Its C64 releases include several familiar coin-op names alongside original home-computer titles.
note: Budget re-releases may appear under their own credited label rather than being folded into Elite's main total.

summary: Gremlin Graphics developed and published a broad range of British computer games, including platformers, sports, racing and character-led action titles across the C64 and Amiga years.
note: The archive keeps later company-name variations separate where they were recorded as distinct publisher credits.

summary: MicroProse became synonymous with detailed simulations and strategy games supplied with substantial manuals, maps and reference material. Its C64 catalogue rewards patience and preparation more than quick arcade play.
note: The CCG archive uses MicroProse Software as the recorded publisher name for these entries.

summary: Rainbird was Telecomsoft's premium label, associated with ambitious adventures, simulations and large-format releases that often included extensive supporting material.
note: Rainbird and Firebird are linked here for context but remain separate publisher archives.

summary: Virgin Games published and distributed a varied computer-game catalogue across the 1980s and 1990s, spanning original titles, conversions and releases from associated studios and labels.
note: Virgin Games and Virgin Mastertronic remain separate because the archive records them as distinct publishing credits.

summary: Thalamus built a focused reputation for technically accomplished Commodore 64 games with strong graphics, music and magazine-era presentation.
note: This summary concerns the games represented in the CCG archive and does not attempt to reproduce a complete company history.
